items.title: Delhi High Court Women Lawyers Forum honours 52 women lawyers for legal aid and pro bono work
items.summary: The Delhi High Court Women Lawyers Forum on Wednesday honoured 52 women advocates for their contributions to legal aid and pro bono work through its first-ever Access to Justice Awards. The awards were organised by the Forum's Legal Aid and Advocacy Group on November 18 at the India International Centre (IIC) Annexe in New Delhi. The theme of the event was 'Women Who Stood Up When It Mattered'. Former Himachal Pradesh High Court Chief Justice Rajiv Shakdher , who presented the awards, noted that the event was an exercise, to give visibility and recognition to a segment of the Bar that is mostly underrated, despite forming a bulwark of both society and the Bar. "What caught my immediate attention was the tagline conceived for the event: women who stood up when it mattered most. Having seen most of them in action both from the bench and in the bar I can without an iota of doubt say that it rings true. These women lawyers have done a phenomenal work which often goes unnoticed. They and their organizations have touched lives , helped marginalized groups and persons with disability without looking for monetary recompense or kudos," Justice Shakdher told Bar & Bench. items.title: All NHRC orders can't be challenged in Delhi merely because its headquarters are here: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday refused to entertain a plea by an Adivasi man from Chhattisgarh alleging that Christian families were forced to flee their village following threats and violence over their refusal to convert to Hinduism [ Baman Ram Kawasi v Union of India & Anr ]. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma held that the Chhattisgarh High Court was the appropriate forum to examine the matter. The petitioner, Baman Ram Kawasi, had approached the High Court challenging the June 9 decision of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) to dispose of his complaint by forwarding it to the District Magistrate (DM) and Superintendent of Police (SP) in Sukma, Chhattisgarh, with directions to take appropriate action within eight weeks. In her judgment, Justice Sharma held that merely because the NHRC passed the order from its headquarters in Delhi, it would not confer territorial jurisdiction on the Delhi High Court to examine a challenge to the NHRC's decision. items.title: Supreme Court questions homebuyers approaching it directly over builder disputes
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday questioned why homebuyers were approaching it directly invoking Article 32 of the Constitution to resolve disputes arising out of failed housing projects, instead of pursuing their remedies before lower courts. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana said it cannot be expected to deal with every dispute between homebuyers and builders. “Please appreciate, under Article 32 (allowing litigants to approach Supreme Court directly for relief when fundamental rights are violated), how many such matters are we going to resolve? Every dispute against a builder, every failed project, will end up here. How are we going to resolve it?” CJI Kant remarked during the hearing. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Court made the observation while hearing a plea by homebuyers over a stalled housing project, seeking protection from recovery proceedings initiated by the State Bank of India (SBI). items.title: Can't order takedown of other courts' orders from internet to protect privacy: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday held that merely because a person is residing in Delhi or able to access judicial orders online from the national capital on the internet does not confer territorial jurisdiction on the Delhi High Court. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma noted that the petitioner wanted de-indexing of an order passed by the Gauhati High Court in a criminal case. “The mere facts that the petitioner resides in Delhi or that the bail order in question is accessible on the internet from Delhi cannot confer territorial jurisdiction upon this Court, when the order sought to be de-indexed has been passed by the High Court of Gauhati, and the entire criminal proceedings, from the registration of the FIR till the discharge of the petitioner, have taken place within the State of Assam. Even otherwise, this Court is of the view that the High Court of Gauhati is the forum conveniens for adjudication of the grievance raised by the petitioner,” the Court observed. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma The petitioner had sought directions to Google and Indian Kanoon to remove a 2019 bail order from name-based search results associated with his name. items.title: Cauvery water dispute: Supreme Court rejects plea by Tamil Nadu for release of additional water by Karnataka
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed the Tamil Nadu government's applications seeking the release of additional water from the Cauvery river in Karnataka. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh passed the order. "We have dismissed (the application)," the Court said, pronouncing the order. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh Tamil Nadu government had filed two applications seeking directions for the immediate release of its due share of Cauvery water. In August, the State had alleged that it did not receive its allocated share from Karnataka despite facing a rain-deficient year. It submitted that due to a shortfall of about 11 thousand million cubic feet (TMC), it was unable to supply any water for irrigation. However, the Karnataka government denied the allegations, stating that it was complying with the orders of the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA). The dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu over Cauvery water dates back to two agreements in 1892 and 1924 between the erstwhile Madras Presidency and the Princely State of Mysore. items.title: Ariyil Shukoor murder: Kerala court acquits CPI(M) leader P Jayarajan and 17 others, convicts 13
items.summary: A Special Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) court in Ernakulam on Thursday (November 19) convicted 13 persons and acquitted 18 persons, including Communist Party of India (Marxist) leaders P Jayarajan and TV Rajesh, in the 2012 Ariyil Shukoor murder case [ State of Kerala v Sumesh KV & ors ]. Shyamjith, son of CPI(M) State Secretary MV Govindan, is among those acquitted in the case. Special CBI court III Judge Sabarinathan P pronounced the verdict while sentencing seven convicts to life imprisonment. Of the 13 persons convicted, 7 were found guilty of murder, 5 were convicted of offences relating to trespass, wrongful restraint and criminal intimidation, while 1 was found guilty of destroying evidence connected to the crime. The 7 convicts found guilty of murder - namely KV Sumeesh (A1) Anoop (A3), Pavithran (A7), Manoharan (A9), MV Dineshan (A10), Bijumon (A12) and Shijin Mohan (A15) - have been sentenced to life imprisonment. They have also been awarded separate sentences for other offences, and their substantive prison sentences would run concurrently. They were directed to be sent to Kannur Central Prison. items.title: Can't ban nightlife; wrong to equate music, dancing in bars to drug menace: Kerala High Court on DJ party curbs
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Monday questioned the basis on which police were targeting DJ parties and night-life in the State, observing that a total ban on such activities is impractical and excessive. [State of Kerala & ors v Mahadevan] A Bench of Justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji was hearing the State’s appeal against a November 10 single-judge ruling that Police cannot impose restrictions on the timings of DJ parties at establishments with appropriate liquor licences that permit their operations during late hours. Justice Ramachandran today questioned the basis for singling out DJ parties, observing that the police’s actions appeared to be based on stereotypes that equate night-life with drug activities. The Court observed that disc jockeying (DJ) is a profession and should be viewed as such. “ Why specifically DJ parties? You have said that they cannot conduct DJ parties. But they can serve liquor there. You have no problem with the consumption of alcohol because the government gets revenue from it … Should we say that nobody can dance in a bar or listen to music?
